title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points and the negation map

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,n), input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256 with the standard generator, recover x; if Q is the identity (the profile's x=0 case) return 0 at once. Algorithm: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points (theta=2^-96), 2^14 lockstep walkers started from 64-bit random coefficients, an r-adding walk with a 2^24-entry table of 64-bit-coefficient points, the negation map (classes of size 2, N'=(n+1)/2), batched affine additions (6M with S=M plus amortised inversion), and fruitless-cycle handling that is a function of the cycle: detection by a fixed 64-step checkpoint holding the full 256-bit canonical u and compared on all limbs every step (a match is a return to that exact class, so a false match would need a 256-bit coincidence, 2^-256 per step, 2^160 below the distinguished-point rate), one lap walked to find the cycle's smallest-u member, and one escape addition from a separate 256-entry table with independent 64-bit coefficients, so merged walks escape together and re-entry into the cycle just left is bounded by its basin at 2^-135.4 per cycle. Success probability at least 0.39 for every walk-quality factor at or above 0.9076 (the collision probability at an ideal random mapping is 0.4199 at k=1.0438 sqrt(N') steps), after subtracting 2^-14 and 10^-10. Total work at most 2^127.82 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification: each walk step is charged 1193 scalar AArch64 instructions (P-256 Montgomery multiplication M=146 and modular add/sub A=21, each counted from an explicit instruction listing with a 5% reserve, plus table index, canonicalisation, coefficient, cycle, distinguished-point and loop work, each itemised as an upper bound), i.e. 1.193 units, over K=(k+2^114.585)/(1-2^-9)=2^127.5648 steps, where 2^-9 bounds the whole fruitless-cycle loss (detected cycles 2^-16.87, re-entry 2^-32.87, undetected cycles longer than 64 classes 2^-9.22). Peak memory at most 2^41 bytes; preprocessing (table, escape table and walker starts, charged for field multiplications and field additions) at most 2^32.9 units, included in total work; nonuniform advice 2^0 bytes. Classical. Heuristics: random-mapping behaviour of the r-adding walk with the negation map (Teske 2001) with the quality margin stated above, the fruitless-cycle counting model and basin bound (Bos et al. 2010; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe 2011), and the bit-field independence of the distinguished-point test from the table index; all disclosed in proof.md. A toy experiment runs the same walk and cycle rule on a toy curve; it is toy-scale support only.

experiments.purpose: Run the walk, the full-width checkpoint cycle rule and the cycle-minimum escape end to end on a toy curve (y^2 = x^3 - 3x + 4 over F_65537, prime order 65851, theta = 2^-6): check scalar recovery by distinguished-point collisions; check that two walkers at one class with different checkpoint histories (one of them possibly inside a cycle) reach the same distinguished point, counting the pairs that instead both loop in one cycle because the escape fell back into its own basin, and any pair that diverges (a non-zero divergence count would refute the merge claim); count escape events and the walkers that came back to the cycle they had just escaped; and report total steps to a collision against sqrt(pi N'/2) with a 95% interval. Toy scope only: it does not establish production cost, walk quality or memory.
